name: README Benchmark
description: Measurements of README composition across 2,069 public GitHub repositories (2,100 sampled; 2,069 had a README), stratified across seven star bands and ten languages, together with the 360 hand-scored labels used to measure the accuracy of those measurements. Features were extracted by regular-expression detectors over markdown, with no language model in the pipeline. Detector accuracy was measured rather than assumed: 360 READMEs were scored by hand against a written rubric with the detector verdicts withheld, across four samples drawn in sequence so that each measured one detector version before that version was changed in response to it. The clean out-of-sample mean F1 is 84.7%, against 92.1% on the samples that shaped the detectors. The study is observational and cross-sectional. Every repository was observed once, and nothing here establishes that a README element caused anything. Sampling is biased toward the top of each star band because GitHub's search API offers no random sampling. The analysed READMEs are deliberately not included: they belong to the projects that wrote them. Every label row names its repository so it can be re-checked. Study page: https://orviqa.dev/research/readme-benchmark
